title: Without injections, flatten() and stream() return the same columns in the same order
rationale: The control that makes the ENRICHED_STREAM comparator able to PASS. Without it the comparator has exactly one fixture, that fixture is a DEFECT, and a comparator that has only ever produced 'not equal' is indistinguishable from a comparator that always produces 'not equal'. This is the good-input leg of the three-way drill. It duplicates the unit test streamMatchesList's claim on purpose, at the corpus level.
catchesBugClass: A traversal divergence between the two entry points introduced by a future refactor - flatten() gaining a sort, or stream() gaining a filter.
cannotCatch: Nothing about ordering under injection, and nothing about memory behaviour, which is stream()'s actual reason to exist. It is a small schema, so it cannot exercise the wide-schema path the streaming API targets.

predicted.detail: Both entry points emit the same three names, and the recorded emission order pins the sequence too.

configDescription: assert ENRICHED_KEYSET vs ENRICHED_STREAM, default FlattenOptions
